questions: What is the result your ideal customers want to achieve?
What are ALL of the other vehicles that they're currently using? (list 8)
What is your new opportunity?
List all your arguments why THIS opportunity is the ONLY way (list 8)

Why don't people want improvement offers — which of the four resistance reasons (improvement is hard, desire vs. ambition, memories of poor past decisions, commodity pricing) hits your market hardest?
Why does your market crave a NEW opportunity instead — which of the four drivers (new discovery, no pain of disconnect, dream replacement, greener pastures) do you lead with?
What 'old vehicle' are you asking your dream customer to abandon, and what 'new vehicle' are you handing them?
concepts: Improvement Vs. Opportunity — Russell Brunson on Dan Kennedy: 'The #1 thing I learned from Dan Kennedy was how to reposition my core offer from repair or improvement to the New Opportunity.' Improvement offers struggle; new opportunity offers convert.

Why People DON'T Want Improvement Offers — four reasons: (1) Improvement is hard, (2) Desire vs. Ambition, (3) Memories of poor past decisions, (4) Commodity pricing. Plus: improvement is tied to Status Increase / Status Decrease dynamics.
Why People CRAVE New Opportunities — four drivers: (1) New discovery, (2) No pain of disconnect, (3) Dream replacement, (4) Greener pastures.

The Vehicle Metaphor — your dream customer is driving an 'old vehicle' toward a result they desire; your job is to hand them a NEW vehicle (new opportunity) that gets them there faster/easier, not to patch up the old one.
What They Really Want — on a scale, 'Improvement' and 'New Opportunity' are not equal. The market's weight always tips toward New Opportunity.
'The greatest business in the world is selling information.' — Russell Brunson
'Whatever the mind can conceive and believe, it can achieve.' — Napoleon Hill
exercises: Define the result your ideal customers want to achieve
List 8 competing vehicles your market is currently using
Define your new opportunity in writing
List 8 arguments why YOUR new opportunity is the ONLY way

concepts: The Stack Slide — the #1 goal of Session #3: create a stack slide that makes your offer irresistible. Structure: 'What You're Gonna Get…' list of Masterclass, Tools, Tangible #1, Tangible #2, Tangible #3, Bonus (Priceless) → Total Value: $X.

Core Principle — 'You have a product, maybe a course, software, or something else. But the product itself is not the offer. The offer is a bunch of products combined to increase the perceived value of the thing you're trying to sell.'

Fast Product Creation Framework — your offer is assembled from 4 categories: (1) Written Word, (2) Spoken Word (Audio + Video), (3) Physical Products, (4) Other Stuff. All four categories feed into 'YOUR OFFER' at the center.
'People Will Spend MORE Money For The Same Product Packaged In A Different Way.' — Russell Brunson
Two-layer brainstorm — (a) what you ALREADY have (dollar-value everything based on time/money invested), (b) what you haven't created YET but could complement your core offer.

Offer Stack structure — 4 to 6 complementary products, each priced, summed to Total Value, with a final 'Get It Today For Only' price that's dramatically lower (creating the 10:1 value-to-price ratio).
